protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 warnings, 2 notes).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 24 stocks
   line 57:  p20.aspirate(2, samples_rack[target_wells[i]])
   At line 57 the tip went into sample 1 (tube A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A2 in slot 2),
   sample 3 (tube A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (tube A4 in slot 2) and 20 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3) and water (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step
   (this line did it 24 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in
   the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there.
   The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left
   in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 57 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [945a4dde438e]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: A mix stroke as big as the well, 8 wells: 15 ul in 12.5 ul
   line 60:  p20.mix(5, 15, plate[target_wells[i]])
   At line 60 the tip mixes wells C5, C6, D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 and D6 in slot 5 with 5 strokes
   of 15 ul in a well holding 12.5 ul (this line did it 8 times). A stroke of the whole well
   draws air at the bottom and foams the liquid. Integra draws over 80% of the well five
   times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: wells C5, C6, D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 and D6 in slot 5.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (10 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 10,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [ad8d47d83014]

3. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (tube A1 in slot 3)
   line 54:  p20.aspirate(12.5, master_mix_rack["A1"])
   At line 54 the tip went into master mix (tube A1 in slot 3) while it still carried water
   (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that
   were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 54 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [e4092c159bb9]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 16 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 55:  p20.dispense(12.5, plate[target_wells[i]])
   At line 55 the robot starts putting master mix into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR
   (slot 5), and 16 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds
   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2
   and 8 more in slot 5.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 8 more in slot 5.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [c876735b7293]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
